sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Trap Bar Squat is a compound lower-body exercise performed by standing inside a hexagonal (trap) bar and squatting while holding the handles at your sides.

The neutral grip and centered load create a more upright torso position than a back squat, reducing stress on the lower back while still driving strong quad and glute development.

It's an excellent squat variation for athletes, beginners, and anyone looking to train the squat pattern with lower spinal load.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- More upright torso than a barbell back squat
- Reduced stress on the lower back
- Neutral grip is easier on wrists and shoulders
- Combines elements of squat and deadlift mechanics
- Great for building quad and glute strength
- Easier to learn than a back squat
- Allows heavy loading with safer mechanics
- Excellent for athletic power development

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Quadriceps, Glutes

Secondary: Hamstrings, Erector Spinae, Core, Trapezius, Forearms and Grip, Calves

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand inside the trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grip the handles with palms facing inwards (neutral grip).
3. Chest up, shoulders back, spine neutral.
4. Stand tall with the bar held at your sides.
5. Eyes forward, neck neutral.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Keep your chest lifted and engage your core.
2. Lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, maintaining a neutral spine.
3. Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as you can comfortably go.
4. Keep your knees in line with your toes throughout the movement.
5. Push through your heels and engage your leg muscles to return to the starting position.
6. Finish upright with hips fully extended.
7. Repeat for the desired reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Knees caving inward during descent or ascent
- Rounding the lower back at the bottom
- Leaning too far forward (turning it into a deadlift)
- Not squatting deep enough
- Rising on the toes instead of driving through heels
- Letting the bar drift forward or backward
- Losing core brace during the lift
- Using momentum instead of controlled reps

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Trap Bar (Hex Bar)
- Weight Plates (bumper or iron)
- Lifting Platform or Suitable Floor Surface
- Optional: Lifting Belt for heavier loads
- Optional: Lifting Straps for grip support
- Optional: Chalk for improved grip
- Recommended: Flat-soled shoes for stability

sections.heading: Choosing Handle Height
sections.content:
1. Most trap bars have high and low handle options.
2. High handles reduce range of motion - easier on back and mobility.
3. Low handles increase depth and leg involvement.
4. Beginners often start with high handles.
5. Taller lifters may prefer high handles to maintain form.
6. Choose the height that allows a deep, upright squat.
7. Stay consistent with your choice to track progress.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, centered inside the bar.
2. Toes: Slightly turned out (10-20 degrees).
3. Grip: Neutral, palms facing each other, firm hold.
4. Torso: Upright with chest up and core braced.
5. Shoulders: Pulled back and down.
6. Knees: Tracking over toes.
7. Head: Neutral, eyes looking forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Barbell Back Squat: Traditional barbell squat variation
- Front Squat: Quad-dominant barbell squat
- Goblet Squat: Dumbbell or kettlebell squat
- Trap Bar Deadlift: Same bar, more hip hinge pattern
- Dumbbell Squat: Holding dumbbells at sides
- Safety Bar Squat: Reduced shoulder strain alternative

sections.heading: Trap Bar Squat Variations
sections.content:
Standard Trap Bar Squat: Full range, neutral grip
High Handle Trap Bar Squat: Reduced range of motion
Low Handle Trap Bar Squat: Increased depth and leg involvement
Paused Trap Bar Squat: Pause at bottom for strength
Tempo Trap Bar Squat: Slow eccentrics for muscle building
Trap Bar Jump Squat: Explosive power development

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Lower Back Pain: Use high handles or lighter loads
Knee Issues: Reduce depth or switch to leg press
Grip Issues: Use lifting straps or chalk
No Trap Bar: Substitute with goblet squats or dumbbell squats
Mobility Restrictions: Use high handles for shorter range
Learning Stage: Start light, focus on knee tracking and upright torso
